description: Proposal of Application Notice and pre-application consultation for 'Proposed Green Data Centre and Relocation of Green Space' at 1 Redheughs Avenue, prepared by Scott Hobbs Planning for Shelborn Drummond Ltd. Public exhibition boards dated 22 May 2025; feedback deadline 11 June 2025.
decision_notes: PAN reference number not located (portal unreachable from research environment).

description: EIA screening request for the proposed data centre at 1 Redheughs Avenue. The council determined that an Environmental Impact Assessment was not required, reasoning that the brownfield urban site is not in a sensitive area, that the development would likely have a negligible impact on national greenhouse gas reduction targets, and that mitigation (waste heat, sustainability, noise, light, design, flood risk, landscaping, ecology) could be secured through the planning application process.
decision_notes: The screening decision was strongly criticised by APRS ('gobsmacking') and was among the matters scrutinised at the committee hearing; the Screening Checklist and Screening Decision Report were later lodged on the DPEA appeal file (8 July 2026).

description: Planning permission in principle for erection of a Green Data Centre with associated infrastructure, landscaping, servicing, car and cycle parking; formation of public park with sports facilities; and formation of active travel routes; full approval for the siting of the data centre development and public park; maximum height and limits of deviation of proposed development; siting of active travel routes and points of vehicular access/egress.
decision_notes: Refused unanimously by the Development Management Sub-Committee on 4 February 2026 against the officer recommendation of approval, after a hearing (data centre debated for nearly two hours of a four-hour meeting); formal decision date 9 February 2026 per the DPEA record. Refusal grounds as summarised by APRS: contrary to NPF4 Policy 1 (climate and nature crises), contrary to NPF4 Policy 2 (failure to address lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions), and contrary to City Plan 2030 Place 19 (does not support the mixed-use vision for the Edinburgh Park/South Gyle area). Committee debate focused on the undefined status of a 'green data centre' under NPF4, unevidenced renewable power supply figures, cooling and water uncertainty, deliverability of waste heat re-use, limited job creation (council consultation-response estimate of 39 jobs against over 200 proposed parking spaces), and impacts (noise, visual, security fencing, generator flues, diesel generator use) on the consented mixed-use development including housing c. 50 m away.

representations.notes: Objection and support counts not established: the Idox portal was unreachable from the research environment and the committee report could not be retrieved. The application was reported to have 'caused uproar' from October 2025 and triggered a pre-determination hearing; 38 representations were separately lodged with the DPEA at appeal stage.

description: Planning permission appeal by Shelborn Drummond Ltd against City of Edinburgh Council's refusal of 25/04239/PPP. Reason for appeal: refusal of application. Procedure: written submissions and further written submissions. Reporter: Ms Sue Bell; case officer Christopher Kennedy.
